explanation: This slide covers simple invertebrates and Radiata. Sponges are the only animals that lack true tissue; they are filter feeders with porous bodies, interior canals lined with flagellated cells, and structural spicules used for species identification. Sponges reproduce both sexually and asexually. Comb Jellies are solitary, free-swimming marine animals (a few cm to 1.5 m long) that move using beating cilia; their body is made of transparent mesoglea, they lack stinging properties (adhering to prey instead), and some are bioluminescent. Cnidarians have stinging cells called cnidocytes, and a body structured as a two-layered sac (the internal digestive cavity also acts as a hydrostatic skeleton). Their body forms are polyp (cup facing up) or medusa (cup facing down), and examples include sea anemone, coral, hydrozoans, jellyfish, and hydra.

questions.q: Which animal group is unique in having no true tissues?
questions.exp: The notes state that Sponges are the 'Only animal to lack true tissue'.

questions.q: What structures do comb jellies use for locomotion, and what substance forms their body?
questions.exp: The notes state that comb jellies 'Use beating cilia to move' and have a 'Body made of transparent jellylike substance – mesoglea'.

questions.q: What are the two body forms of cnidarians, and which cell type is characteristic of them?
opts: Polyp (cup up) and Medusa (cup down); cnidocytes
